newsitem.title: USA: MSRB seeks comment on consultant rule revision.
newsitem.headline: MSRB seeks comment on consultant rule revision.

text.p: The Municipal Securities Rulemaking Board on Thursday requested comment on a proposal to give dealers an alternative way to disclose their consulting arrangements to issuers.

The panel's rule G-38 requires dealers to disclose in writing the name, company, role and compensation arrangement of any consultant that they use, directly or indirectly, to help them get bond business with issuers.
Dealers must make the disclosures before the issuer selects a dealer for a particular offering.

"It has come to the Board's attention that this issue-specific nature of the disclosure requirement can create compliance problems for dealers," said the board, which wants comments on its proposal by August 15.

For example, an issuer may bring new issues to market several times a month, and if a dealer is using a consultant to get a syndicate slot in each issue, the dealer has to disclose the same information monthly, or even weekly, MSRB said.
Also, dealers that use a consultant to help get co-manager business sometimes have difficulty complying with rule G-38, MSRB said.
"Unlike a lead manager, a co-manager may learn of its selection for that business after the selection of the lead manager," MSRB said.
That makes it impossible for the dealer to disclose its consulting arrangements before the issuer selects any dealer, as required by rule G-38, the board said.
The board proposed giving dealers the option of disclosing their consulting arrangements to issuers on either an issue-specific or issuer-specific basis.

Under the proposal, a dealer disclosing on an issuer-specific basis would have to notify the issuer in writing within three business days of the consultant's "first direct or indirect communication with that issuer."
In any case, the dealer would notify the issuer before the issuer selects it for muni business, MSRB said.
Dealers also would have to promptly notify the issuer in writing about any change in the information, and update them annually even when information has not changed, MSRB said.
